documents.t: One Laravel application gives you: the Admin Panel at /admin, where your team runs the platform (its sidebar and title call it Studio); the Creator Portal at /creator, where approved creators upload their series (Creator Portal guide); the REST API at /api/v1, used by the app and the website; share pages (/s/…, /c/…) and your legal pages (/legal/…).
By: WRTeam Project lead and main support: Bhavik Pindoriya, wrteam.bhavik@gmail.com All contacts are on the Support page.

1 Check your server Server requirements: PHP 8.5, MySQL 8, a cron job, and ffmpeg or Cloudflare Stream for videos. 2 Upload and install Upload the code, then run the installation wizard. 3 Start the background jobs Cron and background jobs. Without them no video is processed and no email or push is sent. 4 Fill in the settings Branding, email, storage and video, Firebase, payments, app and support and the rest under Settings. 5 Set your prices Monetization: regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ads and rewards. 6 Go live Follow the go-live checklist.
documents.s: Set it up in this order

documents.t: Many things happen in the background: processing uploaded videos, sending emails and pushes, publishing episodes at their release time, handling store notifications, expiring bonus coins and building reports. All of it starts from one cron job.

Add this line, with your own folder, so it runs every minute: * * * * * cd /home/youruser/edrama && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1 cPanel: Advanced › Cron Jobs › Common Settings: Once Per Minute, and the command above. VPS: crontab -e as the user that owns the files (often www-data). If php on your host isn't PHP 8.5, use its full path, for example /usr/local/bin/php or the path your host gives for PHP 8.5.

By default the cron job also starts the queue workers every minute (EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=true in .env). Two worker pools run in the background, and each stops when its queues are empty or after 55 seconds: Pool Queues, in priority order Time per job urgent webhooks (store and video notifications), notifications, default (emails and the rest) 60 seconds slow video, reports 600 seconds This needs no long-running process, so it works on shared hosting.
Open Admin Panel›System›System. It shows the queues, the scheduled tasks and when each last ran, and any failed jobs, which you can Retry, Retry all or Delete.

For faster processing on a VPS, run the workers all the time with Supervisor. The backend includes a ready config at docs/deploy/supervisor.conf with four programs: two urgent workers, one default worker, one slow worker for video and reports, and the scheduler. 1 Copy the config sudo cp docs/deploy/supervisor.conf /etc/supervisor/conf.d/edrama.conf Edit it: set APP_DIR to your backend's folder and user= to the user that owns the files. 2 Turn off the cron-started workers In .env, set: EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=false Then run php artisan config:clear. 3 Start Supervisor sudo supervisorctl reread sudo supervisorctl update sudo supervisorctl start edrama:* The Supervisor config runs the scheduler itself (schedule:work), so on that server remove the cron line, or keep the cron line and remove the edrama-scheduler program. Run exactly one of the two. After every update Run php artisan queue:restart so running workers finish their job and load the new code.

All times are UTC. Runs Task Every minute Publish episodes whose release time has passed; send scheduled pushes Every 5 minutes Expire bonus coins; send pushes held during quiet hours Every 10 minutes Check videos stuck in processing Every 15 minutes VIP renewal reminders (24 hours before a charge); Top 10 Today; title, Dashboard and Creator Portal statistics Daily Wallet check against the ledger (02:30); Google Play voided purchases (03:30); clean old exports, job runs and unfinished uploads (04:00 to 04:30) Monthly, 1st at 02:00 The monthly creator report (how creators earn)
Run these from the backend's folder, in a terminal or over SSH.

Command What it does php artisan edrama:create-owner Creates the Owner once, if the installer didn't. Refuses when an Owner already exists. Without a terminal it reads EDRAMA_OWNER_NAME, EDRAMA_OWNER_EMAIL and EDRAMA_OWNER_PASSWORD from .env: remove the password once the Owner exists. php artisan edrama:demo-data Imports the demo data. Adds nothing if it's already there. Asks to confirm on a production server (--force skips the question). php artisan edrama:video-webhook Registers the Cloudflare Stream webhook and saves its secret (Storage and video). php artisan edrama:video-status <episode> --refresh Shows one episode's video status, asking the video service again with --refresh. php artisan edrama:move-stream-videos Moves every episode video off Cloudflare Stream (same as the button on Storage & video). php artisan edrama:creator-report --month=2026-10 Builds the monthly creator report for a month again. php artisan queue:restart Makes running workers load new code. Run after every update. php artisan config:clear Run after editing .env.

These run from the cron job (Background jobs). You don't need to run them. edrama:publish-episodes, edrama:send-scheduled-pushes, edrama:expire-bonuses, edrama:release-held-pushes, edrama:vip-renewal-reminders, edrama:rank-top-titles, edrama:roll-up-title-stats, edrama:roll-up-daily-metrics, edrama:roll-up-creator-stats, edrama:wallet-reconcile, edrama:store-voided-purchases, edrama:prune-exports, edrama:prune-job-runs, edrama:prune-video-uploads, edrama:creator-report and edrama:work-queues. caution edrama:wallet-reconcile only reports a wallet that doesn't match its coin history. It never changes anything.

Most settings live in the Admin Panel. A few, which change only when you deploy, are in the backend's .env file. The installer fills in the essential ones. After you edit .env, run: php artisan config:clear Keep it private .env holds your database password and the app key. It must never be reachable from the web: your domain must point at the public folder only (Upload the code).

APP_URL, APP_KEY, APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, the DB_* database settings, SESSION_DRIVER, CACHE_STORE and QUEUE_CONNECTION (all database), EDRAMA_INSTALLER=false and EDRAMA_LICENSE_ENFORCED=true. Leave these as they are unless your server changes.

Key Default What it does EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE, EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256, EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID empty Make share links open your app (Share links) EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED true The cron job starts the queue workers. Set false when Supervisor runs them (Background jobs). EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH, EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH not set Where ffmpeg is, when it isn't on the server's path (Storage and video) EDRAMA_APP_CHECK off Firebase App Check on the app's API: off, monitor (log only) or enforce (Mobile App › Firebase) EDRAMA_APP_CHECK_APP_IDS empty Limit App Check to these Firebase app IDs, comma-separated. Empty allows every app of the project. EDRAMA_DEFAULT_REGION GLOBAL The region code used when none is set as default EDRAMA_COUNTRY_HEADER CF-IPCountry The request header that holds the viewer's country EDRAMA_BONUS_EXPIRY_DAYS 7 A fallback for bonus coin expiry. Set it per region in Monetization › Rewards › Bonus coins expire after. EDRAMA_API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE 300 API requests per minute for each viewer EDRAMA_CORS_ORIGINS empty Extra web origins allowed to call the API from a browser, comma-separated EDRAMA_SUPPORT_EMAIL support@example.com Used until Settings › App & support › Support email is saved. Set one of the two, or the app shows the example address. EDRAMA_ALERT_EMAILS, EDRAMA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL empty Used until Settings › Notifications › System alerts is saved MAIL_* log Server email settings, used until Settings › Email delivery (SMTP) is saved

Key Why EDRAMA_DEMO_MODE Turns both panels read-only with "Sign in as" buttons. Only for a public demo. EDRAMA_FAKE_FIREBASE_TOKENS For local development only. Never on a live server. APP_DEBUG true shows error details to everyone. Keep it false.

Open https://admin.your-domain.com/admin and sign in with the Owner's email and password. The Dashboard, shown here with the demo data. After 5 failed sign-ins in a row, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes. A team session ends 12 hours after sign-in, however active you are. Forgot the password? Use the reset link on the sign-in page. It needs email delivery set up. Open Your account from the sidebar footer to change your name, photo and password, and to set up two-factor authentication. The Owner also edits the Creator profile there: how your platform shows up as the creator of your own and licensed series in the app.

Group Pages Overview Dashboard Content Titles, Categories, Upload & pipeline, Release schedule, Home builder, Website Community Creators, Review queue, Comments & reviews Audience Users, Balance adjustments, Support tickets, Push Money Monetization, Transactions System Settings, Team & roles, Audit log, System, License & updates What each page does is on Features › Admin Panel menus. Team members only see the pages their role allows.

If you ticked Import demo data during installation, the Admin Panel, the app and the website are full of sample dramas, creators, viewers and figures, so you can see how everything works before adding your own.

1 Open Clear demo data As the Owner, open Admin Panel›System›Clear demo data. The page only appears while demo data is imported. 2 Confirm Type CLEAR in capital letters and confirm. Removed: the demo series, categories, creators and viewers with all their coin and purchase rows, demo dashboard figures and demo pushes. Kept: your regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ad and reward settings; every setting, language, role, legal page and email template; the licence and the Owner; anything you created yourself; and the audit log. A demo series that real viewers have already paid for is kept, hidden.

You can import the demo data at any time from the server's terminal: php artisan edrama:demo-data It adds nothing if the demo data is already there. On a production server it asks you to confirm first; add --force to skip the question.

Tick each item as you go. Your progress is remembered in this browser. 0 of 18 doneReset Server meets the requirements (PHP 8.5, MySQL 8, HTTPS)Guide Backend uploaded, domain points at public/, installer finishedGuide Cron job runs every minute, and System shows the scheduler runningGuide SMTP set up and a test email receivedGuide App name, logos, favicon and theme colour setGuide Storage & video ready (ffmpeg, S3 or Cloudflare Stream) and a test episode playsGuide Firebase keys added, Test connection passesGuide Google Play and App Store keys added, store webhooks setGuide Regions, coin packs and VIP plans priced; product IDs match the storesGuide AdMob unit IDs added and server-side verification turned onGuide All seven legal pages written and publishedGuide App versions and store links filled inGuide Share link files show your app (.well-known)Guide Team invited with the right roles; two-factor requiredGuide Website deployed, Website address and refresh secret setGuide App re-branded, pointed at your server and built for releaseGuide Demo data clearedGuide Your first series uploaded, priced and publishedGuide

Open https://admin.your-domain.com/install. The wizard has four steps: Requirements, Purchase code, Database and Owner account. 1 Requirements The wizard checks the PHP version, every PHP extension, and that storage, bootstrap/cache and .env are writable. Anything Missing is marked. Fix it (or ask your host to), then press Check again. 2 Purchase code Enter your Purchase code. Find it on your CodeCanyon downloads page: Where is my purchase code? The code is registered to this domain. One purchase code is for one domain. 3 Database Enter the Site address (your backend's full address, such as https://admin.your-domain.com), and the MySQL Host, Port, Database name, Username and Password. The database must be empty. The wizard tests the connection before it moves on, then writes these settings to .env. 4 Owner account Create the Owner: the Super Admin who can do everything, including managing the team. Enter a Name, a Work email and a Password of 12 characters or more. Tick Import demo data so you can look around first if you want sample dramas, creators, viewers and figures to explore. You can remove all of it later (see First steps). Press Install. Setting up the database can take a minute.

Creates every database table and the reference data: regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ad and reward settings, role templates and default settings. Activates your purchase code. Creates the Owner account. Switches .env to production: APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, database sessions, cache and queue. Links the public storage folder (php artisan storage:link). Closes the installer. From now on /install answers 404. Imports the demo data, if you ticked it. When it's done, Your studio is ready appears. Click Go to sign-in and sign in at /admin with the Owner account.

"Could not connect to the database": check the host (often localhost on shared hosting), port (3306), database name, username and password, and that the user has all privileges on the database. "The install could not finish": the message says why. Fix it and press Install again. What was already set up is kept. "The demo data could not be imported": the install itself finished. The reason is in storage/logs. Import it later with php artisan edrama:demo-data. The purchase code is refused: check you copied the whole code. If it's registered to another domain, contact support. Next: start the background jobs.

Admin Panel›System›License & updates shows your licence (Purchase code, Domain, Buyer, Last checked), the Installed version and the Update history. Only the Owner can activate, reset or upload updates.

Your purchase code is registered to your domain during installation. The Admin Panel and the Creator Portal only open on a domain with an active code. The app, the website and the API keep working whatever the licence check says. The code is checked again at most every 7 days. If the licence server can't be reached, nothing locks. The panels lock only when the code is clearly invalid or registered to another domain.

1 Free the code On the old domain, click Reset purchase code. Both panels there lock until it's activated again. 2 Activate it on the new domain Open the Admin Panel on the new domain and Activate with the same purchase code.

Updates come as a zip from CodeCanyon, holding version_info.json and source_code.zip. 1 Back up Back up your database and your storage folder first. Run the update at a quiet time. 2 Upload the update Click Upload update and choose the update zip. Files are replaced and new database migrations run. Every file it replaces is backed up first, in storage/app/private/updates. 3 Restart the workers php artisan queue:restart Updates go one version at a time: an update from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 is refused on 1.0.0, so apply each one in order. An update never touches your .env or your uploaded files in storage.

Where: Admin Panel›Money›Monetization Everything viewers pay for is set per region. Pick the region with the Region switch at the top; the tabs then show that region's settings, with prices in its currency. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

The Regions tab. The demo data adds a few regions beyond Global and India. Every country belongs to one region. A country no active region lists uses the default region and its prices. eDrama starts with two: Region Currency Coin value Unlock ads per day Global (default) USD 1 coin = 0.0099 6 India INR 1 coin = 0.29 20 Field What it is Name, Code The code is capital letters, digits and underscores, such as JP. It can't change later. Currency ISO 4217, such as USD. It can't change later: prices, purchases and reports are stored in it. Coin value What one coin is worth in the currency, with up to six decimals. The app shows every price in coins and in money before each unlock, and reports use it to turn coins into money. Time zone The region's time zone. Countries ISO 3166-1 countries. Choosing a country another region lists moves it here. Active Off sends its countries to the default region for new sessions. A New region starts as a copy of the default region's coin packs, VIP plans, title prices, ad limits and rewards, with money prices converted at the two coin values. Review them, then turn it on. Make default changes which region serves every other country. Viewers keep the prices they already locked. Where the country comes from The backend reads the viewer's country from the CF-IPCountry header, which Cloudflare adds when your domain runs through Cloudflare's proxy. To read another header, set EDRAMA_COUNTRY_HEADER in .env. Without a country, viewers get the default region.

The packs viewers buy in the app's coin store. eDrama starts with five per region: Coins Bonus Global (USD) India (INR) Flag 300 +300 1.99 99 First top-up (once per account) 500 +50 4.99 199 1,000 +200 9.99 399 Popular 2,000 +600 19.99 799 5,000 +2,000 49.99 1999 Best value These are starting values. Change them to your own prices. Paid coins never expire. Bonus coins expire after the days set on Rewards and are always spent first. Google Play product ID and App Store product ID must match consumable products you create in Play Console and App Store Connect. Each store sets its own price tiers per country, so set the store prices to match. A pack someone bought can't be deleted: turn off Shown in the app instead.

Weekly, monthly and yearly subscriptions that unlock every drama with no ads. Starting prices: 5.99, 19.99 and 119.99 USD (Global); 49, 149 and 999 INR (India). Field What it is Price In the region's currency Offered in the app Show or hide the plan Google Play subscription ID, Google Play base plan ID From Play Console. Use the base plan itself, never an offer. App Store product ID From App Store Connect Perks One perk per sentence or line, as the app lists them How to create these subscriptions in each store: VIP subscriptions. Locked subscription rules: no free trial that turns into a charge, a renewal reminder 24 hours before every charge, cancel in two taps in the app, and VIP never sees an ad.

Rewarded ads from Google AdMob, used two ways: one ad unlocks one episode, and Rewards ads pay bonus coins. Field What it is Unlock ads per day, Rewards ads per day Daily limits per viewer in this region Coins per Rewards ad 15 by default Maximum ad length Never more than 30 seconds Unlock and Rewards ads share one daily limit Off: each ad unit has its own limit Unlock ad unit ID, Rewards ad unit ID Your two rewarded ad units, in the format ca-app-pub-0000000000000000/0000000000 Turn on server-side verification In AdMob, open Ad units › each unit › Server-side verification and set the callback URL to https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/admob-ssvCopy. An ad unlocks an episode or pays coins only once AdMob confirms it there. Locked ad rules: 1 ad = 1 reward, at most 30 seconds, no playable or interactive ads in the unlock path, VIP never sees ads, and ads never auto-play an unlock.

Spin wheel: the prizes in the order they sit on the wheel (an even number of them), each with Coins and a Weight (its chance compared with the others). Every spin pays. The screen shows the average spin and about how many coins a daily viewer earns a month. VIP spin multiplier: VIP viewers get the prize times this number (2 by default). Streak titles: earned at a viewer's best streak and kept for good. A title's Bonus coins are paid once. Streak shields: a shield covers one missed day. One shield every (7 days by default) and Most a viewer holds (2). Welcome bonus: coins for new viewers (100 by default) and Days to use them (7). Bonus coins expire after: counted from the day they're earned (7 days by default). Bonus coins are spent before paid coins, earliest expiry first, and they never count towards creator earnings.

These are locked so a pricing change can't quietly undo them: The price is shown in coins and money before every unlock. Price lock: once a viewer starts a series, their per-episode price can't rise. The cost to finish is on every series page. Auto-unlock is off by default and always capped. A daily spend cap (300 coins by default). An append-only coin history the viewer can see. Unlocks belong to the account and come back on a new phone. VIP: a reminder before renewal, cancel in two taps, no ads.

Each series' Coin price per episode and Series Pass price are set per region on the series itself, in Admin Panel›Content›Titles › the series › Prices. A region without its own price uses the default region's. See Features › Coins and unlocks.
The installation wizard checks these for you and highlights anything missing.

Requirement Details PHP 8.5.0 or newer PHP extensions bcmath, ctype, curl, fileinfo, gd, intl, json, mbstring, openssl, pdo_mysql, sodium, tokenizer, xml, zip Writable the storage and bootstrap/cache folders, and the .env file Database An empty MySQL 8 database, with its user and password HTTPS An SSL certificate on your domain. The app and the website only talk to https:// servers. Cron One cron job that runs every minute (Background jobs) Recommended: the pcntl extension, so a stuck background job is stopped after its time limit. The backend is built on Laravel 13 and Filament 5.

Every uploaded episode is turned into adaptive streaming video (1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p). Something has to do that work: Option What you need Good for This server (the default) ffmpeg on the server, and PHP's proc_open function allowed Getting started and small catalogues Amazon S3 ffmpeg on the server, plus an S3 bucket (or S3-compatible: MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi) Growing catalogues: storage grows without filling your disk Cloudflare Stream A Cloudflare account with Stream. No ffmpeg needed. No video work on your server. Cloudflare bills for minutes stored and watched. You choose in Settings › Storage & video, and you can switch later.

Both work. VPS (recommended for video): install ffmpeg with sudo apt install ffmpeg. You can run the background workers with Supervisor for the fastest processing (Background jobs). Shared hosting (cPanel): eDrama runs its background jobs from the single cron job, so no long-running process is needed. For video, either set up a ready-made ffmpeg in your home folder or use Cloudflare Stream. Choose PHP 8.5 in cPanel's MultiPHP Manager (or Select PHP Version). Shared hosting and long videos Transcoding needs CPU and memory. If your host stops long jobs ("Killed" or "Cannot allocate memory"), use Cloudflare Stream or move to a VPS.

Episode files upload in 8 MB chunks, so PHP's upload_max_filesize and post_max_size only need to be above 8 MB. The largest episode file is set in Settings › Video pipeline (up to 200 GB), and the longest episode is 15 minutes.
Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support Everything here reaches the app at its next start, without a new release.

For Android and iOS: Field What it does Latest Your newest version in the store. Minimum supported Builds below it must update before they can be used: the app shows its update screen. Can't be newer than Latest. Store link Your app's Google Play or App Store page. The app's update screen and the website's store buttons use it.

Where viewers and creators write when they need help. It shows in the app's help screen, in creator emails and to suspended creators. Leave it blank to use EDRAMA_SUPPORT_EMAIL from .env, which is support@example.com until you change it, so set one of the two.
A comment or review containing one of these words or phrases waits for a person on Admin Panel›Community›Comments & reviews. Whole words, any case. Press Enter after each.

Switch a feature off and the app hides it at its next start. Switch What it controls VIP Subscriptions that unlock every drama Series Pass One price for a whole series Auto-unlock Unlocks the next episode with coins as it starts Rewards (daily spin and ads for coins) The daily spin, streak titles and Rewards ads Phone sign-in Phone number sign-in, in the app and on the Creator Portal Episode comments Comments under episodes Series reviews Ratings and reviews on series pages

Turn on Show the maintenance screen and write a Message (up to 280 characters, such as when you'll be back). While it's on, the app shows the maintenance screen with your message instead of the catalogue.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Branding One place sets your brand for the app, the Admin Panel, the Creator Portal and the website. A preview of the app and the Admin Panel sits beside the form. Field What it is App name, Tagline Your product's name and one-line tagline. The app shows the name once it reaches the server. Horizontal logo for dark backgrounds A logo with a light name. It replaces the mark and name in the sidebar and on the share and error pages. Horizontal logo for light backgrounds A logo with a dark name, for the top bar and public pages in the light theme. Vertical logo The mark above the name, with a light name, for the dark sign-in screens. Favicon The small icon on the browser tab. Square, at least 64 × 64 pixels. Square logo The mark alone, for small spots such as the push preview. Wordmark font Instrument Serif Italic or Geist Bold, for the name where it's written out. Theme colour One colour for the app, the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal: buttons, switches, progress and highlights. Pick Greenlight (default), Ember, Iris, Rosé, Aqua, Gold, Sky, or a Custom colour by hex code. Text on it switches between ink and white so it stays readable. Studio opens in The theme the Admin Panel and Creator Portal open in: Paper (light), Ink (dark) or Follow the device. Each member can still switch with the moon icon. Logos are PNG or WebP, up to 1 MB, on a transparent background. The app's own logo The logo inside the app (splash screen, Home header) ships with the app. Change it in the app's code: see Mobile App › Logo and icons. The app picks up the App name and Theme colour from here at its next start.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Sign-in screen sets the stage beside the Admin Panel's and the Creator Portal's sign-in forms. Photos: the built-in photos, or up to 3 of your own landscape photos (JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 4 MB each; 1600 × 1000 or larger looks best). Drag to set their order. Motion: Cinematic (photos cross-fade and drift, posters scroll, the tagline rises word by word), Subtle (only the photos cross-fade) or Still. Anyone whose device asks for less motion always gets a still stage. Show the live titles' posters: a strip of your newest live series beside the photos. Words: the tagline and the line under it, separately for the Admin Panel's and the Creator Portal's sign-in.
eDrama sends team invites, password resets, creator emails and system alerts. Until you add an SMTP server, emails are only written to the server's log and nobody receives them.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP) shows how email is sent right now. Add your mail provider's SMTP details on the SMTP server card: Field What to enter SMTP host Your provider's SMTP server, such as smtp.gmail.com or the host your hosting company gives Port Usually 587 with STARTTLS, or 465 with SSL/TLS Encryption STARTTLS (port 587), SSL/TLS (port 465), or None (only for a mail server on your own private network) Username, Password The mailbox login. For Gmail and Google Workspace, use an app password, not the account password. From address The address emails come from, such as no-reply@your-domain.com From name Optional. The sender name people see. Your app's name when empty. Click Send test email to check it. The details are stored encrypted, and they take over from any MAIL_* values in .env. Emails go out through the queue Emails are sent by the background jobs. If they don't run, emails wait. Saving new SMTP details restarts the workers so they use them.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Email templates lists the emails sent to your team and to creators. For each one you can Preview it, Send test, Customize its wording, and Reset it to the default. Editable parts: Subject, Greeting, Text before the button, Button, Text after the button and Sign-off. Markdown works (**bold**, *italic*, [links](https://…)), and the placeholders listed on the form are filled in for you. The button always links to the right page.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Notifications. eDrama uses one Firebase project for the app, the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal: viewers and creators sign in with Firebase Authentication, and pushes go out through Firebase Cloud Messaging. Create the Firebase project first Creating the project, adding the Android and iOS apps and running flutterfire configure are covered in the Mobile App › Firebase guide. Use the same project here.

Click Add keys (or Replace keys) on the Firebase card. Field Where to find it Project ID Firebase console › Project settings › General › Project ID Service account JSON Firebase console › Project settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key. Upload the downloaded JSON file. Web API key Needed for the Creator Portal's sign-in. Project settings › General › Your apps: add a Web app if you have none, and copy its apiKey. Auth domain Needed for the Creator Portal's sign-in, such as your-project.firebaseapp.com (the web app's authDomain). Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave a field empty to keep its current value. Press Test connection after saving.

Field What it does Maximum per viewer per day Pushes above this wait for the next day. The in-app inbox still gets every message. Quiet hours start / Quiet hours end In each viewer's own time. Pushes wait until quiet hours end. The app reads these at its next start. Pushes need the background jobs running.

Who hears within minutes when a background job or scheduled task fails. Alert emails: one or more addresses, separated by commas. Members who can edit Settings also get a bell notification in the Admin Panel. Slack webhook URL (optional): an incoming webhook for your team's alerts channel (Slack › Apps › Incoming Webhooks).

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Legal pages Seven pages, shown in the app and on the website: Terms of service Privacy policy Creator terms (creators accept these before they upload) Content licences & credits Refund policy Community guidelines Takedown requests (DMCA) Edit a page, write its Title and Text in Markdown (headings, lists and links show in the app), and Publish. Each publish adds a new version and keeps the earlier ones, so what a viewer agreed to can be shown later. Each page is public at /legal/<page> on your Admin Panel's domain. Search & sharing on each page sets an optional search title and description per language, or hides the page from search engines. Write your own legal text Store reviewers check that your privacy policy and terms describe your app. Have them written for your business and country.
Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Sign-in & security The Owner can make two-factor authentication required for every team member. See Team and roles.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Payments Coins and VIP are sold through Google Play and the App Store. The backend checks every purchase with the store before it adds coins, and the stores tell it about renewals, refunds and chargebacks. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

Field What it does Default creator share The percent of paid coin revenue a creator earns on their series. A creator's own percent, set on their page in Admin Panel›Community›Creators, wins. Google Play fee, App Store fee The stores' cut, in percent (15 by default). Used to work out net revenue. Reason for the change Recorded in the audit log. The share and fees are saved on each unlock and purchase, so a change never rewrites past money: new unlocks and purchases use the new values. How the numbers combine is explained, with a calculator, on How earnings work.

What a creator may charge per episode, and the free episodes every creator series starts with: Lowest coin price, Highest coin price (30 and 90 coins by default) and Free episodes at least (5 by default).
The daily coin caps a viewer can choose in the app (Choices, in coins: 100, 300, 600 and 1,000 by default) and the Default cap (300). The cap is a fair-play rule and is always on.
Approval limit: when a team member adds or removes more coins than this (1,000 by default), a second member must approve the change.

1 Create a service account In the Google Cloud console, in the project linked to your Play Console (Play Console › Setup › API access), create a service account and download a JSON key for it. Enable the Google Play Android Developer API for the project. 2 Give it access in Play Console Play Console › Users and permissions › Invite new users: add the service account's email with View financial data and Manage orders and subscriptions, for your app. 3 Add the keys On the Google Play card, add the Package name (your app's ID, such as com.yourcompany.yourapp) and the Service account JSON. 4 Turn on real-time notifications So renewals, cancellations and refunds reach eDrama at once: In Google Cloud Pub/Sub, create a topic. Give google-play-developer-notifications@system.gserviceaccount.com the Pub/Sub Publisher role on it. Create a push subscription on the topic, with the endpoint https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/google-playCopy. Turn on authentication, pick a service account, and set the audience to the same URL. Enter that service account's email in Pub/Sub push service account. Google Play notifications are refused without it. In Play Console › Monetize with Play › Monetization setup › Real-time developer notifications, enter the topic's full name and send a test notification.

1 Create an In-App Purchase key App Store Connect › Users and Access › Integrations › In-App Purchase: generate a key and download the .p8 file (you can download it only once). Note the Key ID and the Issuer ID shown on that page. 2 Add the keys On the App Store card, add the Issuer ID, Key ID, Private key (.p8), Bundle ID (your app's bundle ID) and Environment: Production for the live app, Sandbox for TestFlight and test purchases. 3 Add the server notifications URL App Store Connect › your app › App Information › App Store Server Notifications: choose Version 2 and paste https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/app-storeCopy for both production and sandbox. Press Test connection on each card after saving. Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.

Coin packs are consumable in-app products and VIP plans are auto-renewable subscriptions. Create them in Play Console and App Store Connect with the same product IDs you enter in Monetization. Coin packs: the common in-app purchase guide. VIP plans: VIP subscriptions, step by step for both stores.
Admin Panel›System›Settings›Regions & languages.

The app ships in English only. Every other language is a JSON file you upload here, and the app downloads it at its next start, with no new app release. The same screen also offers languages for the Admin Panel. Each language has two files: one for the mobile app and one for the Admin Panel. Hindi is already on A fresh install lists Hindi as offered in the app, without its app file. Upload its file, or edit it and turn off Offered in the app, before you launch. 1 Add the language Click Add language and fill in the Code (such as hi, or a regional code such as pt-BR; it can't change later), the Name and the Native name (how the language picker shows it, such as हिन्दी). Tick Right to left (RTL) for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and the like: the app and the Admin Panel turn their layout around. 2 Translate the file Download the Sample JSON: the English file with every key. Translate the values, never the keys, and keep words in braces such as {name} exactly as they are. 3 Upload it Open Files for the language and upload the app's JSON file (UTF-8, up to 1 MB, plain text only). Keys a file leaves out stay in English. Upload an Admin Panel file too if your team should use the Admin Panel in that language. 4 Turn it on Edit the language and tick Offered in the app. A language can only be turned on once it has its app file. Make default sets the language new viewers start in, and anyone whose phone language isn't offered. Studio language sets the language the Admin Panel opens in for everyone who hasn't picked their own in the top bar. Every upload is a new version. Versions › Make current rolls back to an earlier one.

Your regions can sell in different currencies. The Dashboard and totals are shown in one Reporting currency (USD by default), and refund limits are compared in it. Add an exchange rate for each currency a region uses: Currency, Rate (how much one unit is worth in the reporting currency, up to six decimals) and Valid from. A rate applies from its date until a newer one starts. Rows in a currency with no rate are left out of reporting totals until you add one.
Countries, currencies, coin values, prices and ad limits per region are set in Monetization › Regions.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Storage & video Pick where your images, documents and episode videos live, and who turns uploaded videos into streaming video. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

Each option shows what it needs. Here ffmpeg is found, and S3 and Cloudflare Stream still need keys. Option Images and documents Episode videos You need Local storage (default) This server's disk Transcoded here with ffmpeg, streamed through signed links ffmpeg on the server Amazon S3 Your S3 bucket Transcoded here with ffmpeg, then stored and streamed from S3 through signed links ffmpeg, and S3 bucket keys Cloudflare Stream Stay where they are Cloudflare uploads, transcodes and streams them Cloudflare Stream keys. No ffmpeg. Each card shows whether it's Ready or Needs setup, and what's missing. Videos are made in 1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p, and the app picks the quality for each viewer's connection.

Moving between this server and Amazon S3 copies every file first, in batches, checks each copy, and switches only when all of them are there. The page shows the progress, and you can Retry failed files, Resume or Cancel move. Nothing is ever deleted from where it was, and links in the app keep working throughout. Changing who handles videos applies to new uploads. Videos already uploaded keep playing from where they are. Leaving Cloudflare Stream? Move videos off Cloudflare Stream downloads each video, transcodes it here and stores it with your other files. Viewers keep playing the Stream video until its copy is ready. While Amazon S3 holds your files, its bucket, region and endpoint can't change. Keys can be replaced at any time.
sudo apt install ffmpeg Reload the Storage & video page. It shows ffmpeg 7.x on this server (or your version) in green.

On cPanel you can't install programs, but you can download a ready-made ffmpeg into your home folder. Run these in cPanel › Terminal (or over SSH). 1 Check the server allows it php -v php -r 'var_dump(function_exists("proc_open"));' uname -m You need PHP 8.5, bool(true), and x86_64. If proc_open is false, remove it from disable_functions in cPanel › Select PHP Version › Options (or MultiPHP INI Editor), or ask your host. If uname -m prints aarch64, use arm64 instead of amd64 below. 2 Download ffmpeg cd ~ mkdir -p ffmpeg cd ffmpeg wget https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/releases/ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz tar -xf ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz --strip-components=1 chmod +x ffmpeg ffprobe rm ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz ~/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -version No wget? Use curl -LO with the same address. 3 Check the hosting can transcode ~/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=1080x1920:rate=25 -t 2 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast ~/ffmpeg/test.mp4 && echo "ENCODE OK" rm -f ~/ffmpeg/test.mp4 ENCODE OK means it can. "Killed" or "Cannot allocate memory" means the hosting is too small for video: use Cloudflare Stream or a VPS. 4 Tell eDrama where ffmpeg is In your backend's folder: grep -q '^EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH=' .env || echo "EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH=$HOME/ffmpeg/ffmpeg" >> .env grep -q '^EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH=' .env || echo "EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH=$HOME/ffmpeg/ffprobe" >> .env php artisan config:clear php artisan optimize 5 Check it Refresh Storage & video: the ffmpeg line turns green within a minute. Then upload one short episode in Admin Panel›Content›Upload & pipeline. It should go Uploading → Processing → Ready within a few minutes. The backend's docs/deploy/ffmpeg-shared-hosting.md has the same steps with more troubleshooting.

Create a bucket and an IAM user with access to it in the AWS console, then add its keys under Connections › Amazon S3 bucket: Field What to enter Access key ID, Secret access key The IAM user's access key Region The bucket's region, such as eu-central-1 Bucket The bucket name Endpoint Only for an S3-compatible service (MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi). Leave empty for Amazon S3. Public URL Optional. Where media can be read publicly, such as a CloudFront domain, or the bucket URL with a policy allowing media/*. Empty: media is served through signed links that last six days. Media goes under media/, and private files and videos under files/. Then choose Amazon S3 and confirm. If you use the website, add the bucket's host to its EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS (Website › Connect).

1 Turn on Stream In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Stream and subscribe. Note your Account ID (shown on the account's overview page) and your Customer subdomain (customer-….cloudflarestream.com, shown on the Stream pages). 2 Create an API token My Profile › API Tokens › Create Token › Custom token, with the permission Account › Stream › Edit for your account. Copy the token. 3 Create a signing key Signed playback stops anyone from playing your videos outside the app. Create a key with Cloudflare's API: curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/stream/keys" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>" The answer has an id (the Signing key ID) and a pem (the Signing key). Copy both. The pem can be pasted as Cloudflare returns it. 4 Add the keys Under Connections › Cloudflare Stream, add the Account ID, API token, Signing key ID, Signing key and Customer subdomain. Press Test connection. 5 Register the webhook Cloudflare tells eDrama when a video is ready through a webhook. From the backend's folder, run: php artisan edrama:video-webhook It registers https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/videoCopy with Cloudflare and saves the Webhook secret it returns. Pass a different address as an argument if your Admin Panel's address differs. 6 Switch Choose Cloudflare Stream and confirm. New uploads go to Cloudflare from now on. To check one episode's video from the terminal: php artisan edrama:video-status <episode-id> --refresh.
Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Video pipeline Where videos are stored and processed is set on Storage & video.

Episode files go from the browser straight to where videos live, as MP4, MOV or MKV. Largest file: larger files are refused before they upload. 20 GB to start, up to 200 GB. Allow YouTube videos as episodes: adds Add YouTube video for your team and creators. These episodes are always free, because YouTube doesn't allow charging for them. Turning this off keeps those already added.

Limits for creators in the Creator Portal: Field What it does Largest file a creator uploads 2 GB to start, up to the team's limit above Episodes a creator has processing at once 10 to start. More wait until one finishes. Earliest release after approval A creator's release time must be at least this many hours after your team approves the episode. 0 allows any time from now. 2 hours to start.

When a viewer shares a series or a creator, the app makes a link like https://admin.your-domain.com/s/12 or /c/handle. On a phone with your app installed, that link should open the app. For that, Android and iOS check two files on the link's domain, which the backend serves for you once it knows your app: https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android) https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS) On phones without the app, the link opens a share page with your store buttons.

1 Find your Android signing fingerprints You need the SHA-256 fingerprint of every key that signs your app: Google Play App Signing (most apps): Play Console › your app › Test and release › App integrity › App signing: copy the SHA-256 of the App signing key certificate. Your upload key too, if you also install release builds outside Google Play: keytool -list -v -keystore your-upload-key.jks -alias your-alias 2 Find your Apple app ID It is your Team ID and bundle ID joined by a dot, such as ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.yourapp. The Team ID is in Apple Developer › Membership details. 3 Add them to .env .env EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE=com.yourcompany.yourapp EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256=AA:BB:CC:...,11:22:33:... EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID=ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.yourapp Separate several SHA-256 fingerprints with commas. Then run php artisan config:clear. 4 Match the app The app's share domain must be this domain. See Mobile App › Deep links.

Open both .well-known addresses above in a browser. Each should show your package name or app ID. Empty values mean the .env lines are missing. The website serves the same files from your app settings, so its /series/… and /creators/… pages open the app too (Website › Languages and app links).
Your team signs in to the Admin Panel. Each member has one role, and each role allows None, View or Edit in each area. Manage both in Admin Panel›System›Team & roles.

You have two ways: Invite: enter their email and role. They get an email link to set their own password. The link works once and for 7 days. Needs email delivery. Add member: set a Temporary password (at least 12 characters) and share it with them securely. They must choose their own password at their first sign-in. You can later Change role, Disable (they are signed out on their next click) and Enable a member. Every change is recorded in the audit log.

The Owner can do everything and is the only one who manages the team and edits roles. Four ready-made roles come with eDrama, and you can create your own with New role. Role What it can do Admin Everything except team access; the audit log is view only. Refunds up to 100.00 in your reporting currency. Content Manager Titles, uploads and the release schedule; can look at the review queue. Moderator The review queue and creators. Finance & Support Users, balance adjustments and refunds; can look at transactions and prices. Refunds up to 20.00. Give it Transactions › Edit if it should receive the monthly creator report. The areas a role can be given are: Titles & episodes, Uploads, Schedule & Home, Review queue, Creators, Users, Balance adjustments, Refunds, Transactions, Prices & coin packs, Push, Settings, Team & roles, and Audit log.

Each member can turn on two-factor sign-in in Your account, with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password and the like). They get 8 recovery codes. To make it required for everyone, the Owner turns it on in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Sign-in & security. Team & roles shows who has it on.
Admin Panel›System›Audit log records every action the team takes: who did what, and when. Rows can't be edited or deleted.

A domain or sub-domain for the backend, such as admin.your-domain.com, with SSL. An empty MySQL 8 database, its user and password (create them in cPanel › MySQL Databases, or with your host's tools). Your CodeCanyon purchase code.

1 Unzip the download Unzip the file you downloaded from CodeCanyon. The backend is a Laravel project: it has app, public, vendor folders and an artisan file. Everything it needs, including vendor/, is already inside. You don't need to run Composer or npm. 2 Upload it Upload the backend's files to a folder on your server, for example /home/youruser/edrama. Upload hidden files too (the .env file), and keep the folder structure as it is. 3 Point the domain at the public folder Set your domain's document root to the backend's public folder, for example /home/youruser/edrama/public. cPanel: Domains › your domain › Manage › Document Root. Nginx: root /home/youruser/edrama/public; with requests passed to index.php, as in Laravel's Nginx guide. Only the public folder should be reachable from the web. The .env file and the rest of the code must not be. 4 Open your domain Open https://admin.your-domain.com/install to start the installation wizard. Continue with the installation wizard.

[Initial release] Flutter viewer app for Android and iOS: guest mode, vertical player with adaptive streaming, unlocks with coins, one ad, Series Pass or VIP, wallet, coin store, rewards, library, search, creator profiles and notifications [Initial release] Admin Panel: titles, categories, uploads, release schedule, Home builder, creators and review queue, users, support tickets, push, monetization per region, transactions, settings, team and roles, audit log [Initial release] Creator Portal for approved creators, with review of every episode [Initial release] Public website, edited from the Admin Panel, in several languages [Initial release] Video on this server with ffmpeg, on Amazon S3, or on Cloudflare Stream [Initial release] Web installer, licence activation and update packages

The Creator Portal at https://admin.your-domain.com/creator lets approved creators publish their own series on your platform. Creators upload episodes from their browser, set prices and release times within your limits, follow every review, and see how their series do. Every episode is reviewed by your team before it goes live. From Code to Live — Hassle-Free Installation Service Skip the struggle — we'll set up your app or script, so you can focus on business. documents.t: Someone applies or is invited to become a creator. Your team approves them in Admin Panel›Community›Creators. They sign in to the Creator Portal with the same account they use in the app: Google, email and password, or phone. They accept your Creator terms, create a series, upload episodes and send it for review. Your team approves, asks for changes or rejects it in Admin Panel›Community›Review queue. Approved episodes go live at their release time, and the creator earns their share of paid unlocks (How earnings work).

1 Add the Firebase web keys The portal's sign-in runs on your Firebase project in the browser, so it needs the Web API key and Auth domain in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Notifications › Firebase (guide). 2 Allow your domain in Firebase Firebase console › Authentication › Settings › Authorized domains › Add domain: add your Admin Panel's domain, such as admin.your-domain.com. 3 Turn on the sign-in methods Firebase console › Authentication › Sign-in method: turn on Google, Email/Password and Phone (as you use them in the app). Phone sign-in on the portal also follows the Phone sign-in switch in Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support. 4 Publish the Creator terms Write and publish Creator terms in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Legal pages. Creators can't create a series until they're published. 5 Set the creator limits The price range and free episodes in Payments, and the upload limits in Video pipeline.

Open /creator. The sign-in page shows the sign-in methods. If it says Creator sign-in isn't set up yet, the Firebase web keys are missing. If Firebase says the site isn't allowed, add the domain to Authorized domains.
There are two ways in. Either way, only creators whose status is Active can open the portal.

Anyone can apply at https://admin.your-domain.com/creator/apply. Link to it from your website (the Creators section has an invitation to become one) or your social pages. Applications arrive in Admin Panel›Community›Creators. When your team accepts one, the creator account is made and an invite email is sent.
In Admin Panel›Community›Creators, invite a creator directly by email.

The invite email holds a link to /creator/invite/…. It works for 7 days. The creator opens it, signs in with the account they use in the app (or makes one), and they're in. The account is the app account A creator signs in to the portal with the same Google, email or phone account they use in the app, so their profile in the app and their series stay together.

Status What the creator sees Active The full portal Not a creator "This isn't a creator account yet", with a link to apply Suspended "Your creator account is suspended", with your support email A creator's own revenue share can be set on their page in Creators. Without one, the Default creator share from Payments applies.

This is the creator's side. Share this page with your creators. 1 Accept the Creator terms At the first sign-in, the portal shows the Creator Terms. Tick I have read and agree and Accept and continue. When the terms change, the portal asks again. 2 Create the series New series: the title, synopsis, categories and artwork. The series starts as a Draft. 3 Set the price The coin price per episode, within the platform's limits (30 to 90 coins and at least 5 free episodes by default). The first episodes are always free, so viewers can start the story. 4 Upload episodes and subtitles Upload episodes: drop the video files (MP4, MOV or MKV) straight from the browser. Each one shows its progress as it uploads and processes. Add Subtitles for each episode. If the platform allows YouTube episodes, Add YouTube video adds one by its link. YouTube episodes are always free. 5 Set release times Release times: when each episode goes live. The earliest is a number of hours after the review team approves it, set by the platform. 6 Send it for review Confirm that you have the rights to publish it, and submit. The series shows In review.

The review team can approve, request changes (with the reason), or reject. Each decision shows in Notices and arrives by email, and History lists every status change with the reviewer's reason. Changes requested: see the reason, fix it, and resubmit. Live: approved episodes go out at their release time, or at once if they have none.

Each series has a Stats page. For each episode over the last days, it shows views, the share of viewers who watched to 90%, unlocks by method, and how many went on to the next episode. The portal shows no money figures. Creator earnings are worked out in the monthly creator report and paid by the platform (How earnings work).
Admin Panel›Community›Review queue holds creator submissions and viewers' reports. Team members whose role can edit Review queue work here (the Moderator role, for example).

Assign to me an item, so nobody else works on it at the same time. A colleague can take over if needed. Watch the episodes and check the artwork, prices and rights. Decide: Decision What happens Approve The episodes go live at their release time, or at once if they have none Request changes The creator sees your reason and can resubmit Reject With a reason Unpublish Takes a live episode down, with a reason Mark resolved Closes a viewer's report, with a note Ask the creator to fix it Sends a report on to the creator Each decision writes a notice in the creator's portal and sends them an email.

Coins and unlocks: paid and bonus coins, the ways to unlock, price lock and the spend cap. How earnings work: how a paid unlock turns into store fees, the creator's share and yours. Earnings calculator: try your own prices and volumes.

The backend enforces these, and the Admin Panel can't switch them off: Every price is shown in coins and money before the tap. Price lock: a viewer's per-episode price never rises mid-series. A daily spend cap, and auto-unlock off by default. One ad of 30 seconds or less unlocks one episode. VIP has no free trial trap, a reminder 24 hours before every charge, cancel in two taps, and no ads. An append-only coin history: nothing is deleted, nothing is charged twice, and corrections are added as new rows.
Every page of the Admin Panel, in the order of the sidebar. Team members only see the pages their role allows.
How the platform is doing today: viewers, unlocks, revenue and more, in your reporting currency. Figures refresh every 15 minutes.

Every drama, its episodes, its prices per region and who owns it. A title is one of three kinds: Your own series (an Original), a Licensed series, with the licensor's share of net revenue from your contract, a Creator series, made by an invited creator who earns their share of every paid unlock. Every title starts as a draft: add episodes, artwork and prices, send it to review, then publish. Prices set the coin price per episode and the Series Pass per region; a region without its own price uses the default region's. Price lock keeps the price each viewer started with. Episodes have subtitles, and a series can be marked Complete once every episode is out.
The labels on your titles, and the picks in the app's onboarding. Drag to set the order the app shows them in.
Upload episode files (MP4, MOV or MKV), many at once. Each goes Uploading → Processing → Ready, turned into vertical streaming video in the background. See Storage and video.
Episodes go out at each one's publish time. Drag an episode to move it, and pick the time zone to read the times in.
Build the app's Home from sections: add, set up, drag to reorder, and choose who sees each one. A phone preview updates as you edit.
Your public website's sections, header, footer, look and search settings. Edit, preview, then publish. See Website › Edit the website.
Invited creators, their revenue share, and new applications. See Becoming a creator.
Creator titles, new episodes and viewer reports waiting for a decision. Every decision is logged. See The review queue.
What viewers say about your titles. Check reports, approve what was held by the blocklist, and remove what breaks the rules.

Find a viewer by name, email or ID, and open their profile, wallet and coin history, unlocks, purchases and devices. Wallet changes always need a reason and are logged. From a viewer you can adjust their balance, grant an episode, or ban the account.

Every series starts with free episodes to hook the viewer. After them, each episode is locked until the viewer unlocks it. The number of free episodes is set on the series, and its coin price per episode is set per region in Admin Panel›Content›Titles › the series › Prices.

Paid coins Bonus coins Where from Bought in the coin store The welcome bonus, the bonus in coin packs, the daily spin, streak titles, Rewards ads, team adjustments Expire? Never Yes, after the days set in Monetization › Rewards (7 by default) Spent After bonus coins First, earliest expiry first Earn the creator anything? Yes No The wallet shows both, and every coin in or out is a row in the viewer's coin history. Rows are never edited or deleted. A correction or refund is a new row.

On a locked episode, the unlock sheet shows every option with its price in coins and in the viewer's money: Option What it costs Notes Coins The episode's coin price Bonus coins are used first One ad Watching one rewarded ad to the end Up to the region's daily limit. Paid only once AdMob confirms the ad. Series Pass One coin price for the whole series Can be switched off in Settings › App & support VIP A weekly, monthly or yearly subscription Unlocks every drama, with no ads
When a viewer starts a series, the per-episode price they see is locked for them. If you raise the price later, the rise doesn't reach viewers who already started. A price cut does.

Spend cap: each viewer has a daily coin cap. They choose it from your choices (100, 300, 600 or 1,000 coins by default; 300 to start), and can raise it for the day. Auto-unlock: off by default. When a viewer turns it on, the next episode unlocks with coins as it starts, always within the cap.
The app turns coins into money with the region's coin value. In the Global region one coin is worth 0.0099 USD, so a 60-coin episode shows as about 0.59 USD.

Move the sliders or type numbers to see how one month of a series splits between the stores, its creator (or licensor) and you. It uses the same formulas as eDrama's monthly creator report, with eDrama's starting values filled in. Region Global (USD)India (INR)My own coin value 1 coin = 0.0099 USD (the value eDrama starts with) Who owns the series? A creatorA licensorYou (your own series) Their own share, or the Default creator share (50%). Creator share % One month of the series Coin price per episodeCreators: 30 to 90 by default coins Episodes unlocked with coins Paid with bonus coinsBonus coins earn nothing % Series Passes sold Series Pass price coins Store feeGoogle Play and App Store: 15% by default % Add ad and VIP money Ad and VIP money isn't per unlock: your finance team fills in a monthly pool per region from the AdMob and store reports, and the report splits it by verified ad unlocks and by VIP minutes on locked episodes. Here the series' part is shared at the same percent as coins. This month Coins spent on unlocks 300,000 of which bonus coins (earn nothing) 90,000 Paid coins, with Series Passes 258,000 Gross money $2,554.20 Store fees $383.13 Net money from coins $2,171.07 Creator earns$1,085.54 You keep$1,085.54 Before your own costs (hosting, video, payment taxes). Store fees vary by store and programme; use the fees you actually pay. What this doesn't include Your own running costs: hosting, video storage and streaming (for example Cloudflare Stream's minutes), taxes and payment payouts. Store fees also differ by country and programme; enter the fees you actually pay.

Every series has an owner, and the owner decides who shares its money: Series Who shares the net money Your own (made or bought outright by you) Nobody: you keep it all Licensed The licensor gets their Licensor share, from the contract, set on the series A creator's series The creator gets their own share, set on their page in Creators, or else the Default creator share (50% to start)

Only paid coins earn money. Bonus coins (the welcome bonus, coin-pack bonuses, the spin, streak titles, Rewards ads) are given away, so they earn nobody anything. For each series, each region and each month: paid coins = paid coins spent on its episodes + paid coins spent on its Series Passes gross money = paid coins × the region's coin value net money = gross money × (1 − store fee ÷ 100) owner's money = net money × the owner's share ÷ 100 your money = net money − owner's money Coin value: what one coin is worth in the region's currency (0.0099 USD in Global and 0.29 INR in India to start), set in Monetization › Regions. Store fee: Google Play and App Store keep part of every purchase (15% each to start, in Settings › Payments). The report uses the fees saved on that month's purchases in the region, weighted by amount. Saved at the time: each unlock saves the share in force when it happened, and each purchase saves its store fee. Changing a setting never rewrites past money.

A creator series priced at 60 coins in the Global region. In a month, viewers unlock 1,000 episodes with paid coins: Paid coins 1,000 × 60 = 60,000 Gross money 60,000 × 0.0099 = 594.00 USD Store fees (15%) 89.10 USD Net money 504.90 USD Creator (50%) 252.45 USD You 252.45 USD Try your own numbers in the earnings calculator.
A Series Pass's paid coins count for the series too. The report splits them into a released part (the episodes out when the pass was bought) and a future part, and both are shared at the saved share.

Ad and VIP money doesn't come per unlock, so it's shared from a monthly pool per region: Ads: your finance team fills the report's ad_pool_value column with the month's ad money from the AdMob report. It is split by verified ad unlocks. Failed ads don't count, and neither do the creator's own views or accounts less than 24 hours old. VIP: your finance team fills vip_pool_value with the month's VIP money from the store reports. It is split by VIP minutes on locked episodes, each viewer counted once per episode per month. The creator's own viewing never counts.

On the 1st of every month at 02:00 UTC, eDrama builds the creator report for the month before and sends its link to the team members who can edit Transactions (the Owner and Admin with the ready-made roles; give your finance role Transactions › Edit if it should get it). It's a ZIP with two CSV files: The report: one row per series and region, with the unlocks, paid and bonus coins, Series Pass coins, ad unlocks, VIP minutes, the coin value and store fee used, the net money and the creator's money, also in your reporting currency. The settings sheet: the coin values, store fees, exchange rates and shares used, and how each column is worked out. Payouts are made by you, outside eDrama: your finance team pays each creator from the report. The Creator Portal shows creators their views and unlocks, but no money figures. To build a month's report again: php artisan edrama:creator-report --month=2026-10.
A Flutter app for Android 7+ and iOS 15+, in a dark theme by default with a light theme too. It has four tabs: Home, Library, Rewards and Me.

Guest mode: viewers start watching at once, with no sign-up, and get a welcome bonus of coins (100 coins for 7 days by default). Sign in only when it matters: before a purchase, so coins and unlocks follow them to a new phone. Apple, Google, email and phone sign-in. Guest history and the bonus move into the account. Onboarding: pick favourite genres, then language and data saver. Viewers can skip it.

Home: sections you build in the Admin Panel's Home builder: a hero slider, Continue Watching, rows of series, Top 10 and more. Series page: the artwork and synopsis, the cost to finish, every episode with its state (free, unlocked, locked), More Like This, and reviews. Vertical player: swipe between episodes full screen. Episodes list, Up Next, playback speed, quality, subtitles, likes, comments, and Report a problem. Quality adapts to the viewer's connection, and data saver keeps it lower. Screen protection: screenshots and recordings of the player are blocked on Android, and the video is hidden while the screen is recorded on iOS.

Unlock sheet: on a locked episode, every option with its price in coins and money: coins, one rewarded ad, a Series Pass for the whole series, or VIP. See Coins and unlocks. Coin store: coin packs with bonus coins, a first top-up offer, and restore purchases. VIP: weekly, monthly or yearly plans, with a renewal reminder and cancel in two taps. Wallet: the balance, a readable coin history with every row explained, pending purchases, and the spend cap.
A daily spin that always pays, with a bigger prize for VIP. Streak titles for watching on many days in a row, and streak shields that cover a missed day. Ads for coins (Rewards ads).
Library: Watching, My List and Unlocked. Search and browse by genre. Creator profiles with Follow and their series.
Notifications inbox, and push notifications for new episodes, account and purchases, and offers, with quiet hours. Help: a support form to your team, with a purchase picker for payment questions.

Under Me › Settings: autoplay, auto-unlock, data saver, quality and subtitles; language; theme and accent; haptics; notification switches; sign in, edit profile, sign out and delete account; your legal pages and ad privacy choices.

Offline: an offline banner, and screens the viewer already opened keep showing. Maintenance and update required screens, switched from Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support. Languages: English built in, with more downloaded from the Admin Panel, including right-to-left languages.

documents.s: Set it up in this order

documents.t: Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

Create your AdMob account and add the Android and iOS apps: common guide › Google AdMob. eDrama uses two rewarded ad units: one that unlocks an episode, and one for Rewards (bonus coins). What goes where: What Where AdMob app ID, Android android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml: the com.google.android.gms.ads.APPLICATION_ID value AdMob app ID, iOS ios/Runner/Info.plist: GADApplicationIdentifier Ad unit IDs Admin Panel › Money › Monetization › Ads, per region. Not in the app. Server-side verification AdMob › each ad unit › Server-side verification: https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/admob-ssvCopy Replace the test IDs The app ships with Google's sample test app IDs. Put your own in both files before you release. An ad unlocks an episode or pays coins only once AdMob confirms it on that callback, so server-side verification is required.

The app asks for ad consent with Google's User Messaging Platform. Create the messages in AdMob › Privacy & messaging: a GDPR message for Europe, and an IDFA message (Apple's tracking prompt) for iOS. Viewers can reopen their choices in Me › Settings › Privacy choices.

Coins are consumable products and VIP plans are auto-renewable subscriptions. The Series Pass is paid in coins, so it needs no store product. 1 Create the products In Play Console and App Store Connect, create one consumable product per coin pack (common guide › In-app purchases) and one auto-renewable subscription per VIP plan (VIP subscriptions). 2 Enter the same IDs in the Admin Panel Monetization › Coin packs: Google Play product ID and App Store product ID for each pack. Monetization › VIP plans: Google Play subscription ID, Google Play base plan ID and App Store product ID. 3 Connect the stores Add the Google Play and App Store keys and webhooks so the server can check every purchase: Settings › Payments. The app never decides how many coins a purchase gives: it sends the store's receipt to your server, which checks it with the store and adds the coins. Restore purchases in the coin store claims anything interrupted. To test, use Google Play's licence testers and Apple's Sandbox accounts, and set the App Store card's Environment to Sandbox.

Where it shows Change it in Under the icon on Android android:label in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml Under the icon on iOS CFBundleDisplayName in ios/Runner/Info.plist, or Display Name in Xcode › Runner › General Splash, Home header and share text App name in Admin Panel › Settings › Branding. appName in lib/app/config/app_config.dart is used until the app first reaches the server.
The app's core settings are in one file: lib/app/config/app_config.dartCopy. Edit the values, then build. There are no environments or build flags to set up.

lib/app/config/app_config.dart static const String apiBaseUrl = 'https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/'; static const String shareBaseUrl = 'https://admin.your-domain.com'; Setting What it is apiBaseUrl Your Admin Panel's API, ending in /api/v1/. Must be https://. shareBaseUrl Where shared links point, such as https://admin.your-domain.com/s/12. No trailing slash. It must be the domain that serves the link files: your backend's domain (Deep links).

Setting Default What it does appName 'eDrama' The name on the splash and Home header until the Admin Panel's App name arrives appId 'in.wrteam.edrama' Your Android application ID and iOS bundle ID. Change it when you change the package name: YouTube's player needs it. companyName 'WRTeam' Your company's name, read out for the logo on the splash screen showCompanyLogo true Shows "Made by" your company at the bottom of the splash. Replace assets/branding/company_logo.svg with yours, or set false to hide it. defaultThemeMode ThemeMode.dark The theme a new install starts in. Viewers can change it. defaultAccent AppAccent.greenlight The accent until the Admin Panel sends one (Colours and fonts) followDeviceLanguage true Start in the phone's language when the app has it signInWithGoogle, signInWithApple, signInWithPhone, signInWithEmail true The sign-in methods. Turn off any you haven't set up in Firebase. Apple requires Sign in with Apple on iOS whenever Google is offered. protectScreen true Blocks screenshots and recordings of the player on Android, and hides the video while the screen is recorded on iOS. Turn it off only if your content may be captured freely. Prices, coin packs, VIP plans, ad unit IDs, feature switches, languages and texts are not in the app. They come from the Admin Panel, so you change them without a new release.

To change Edit Colours lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dart Fonts lib/core/theme/app_typography.dart and fonts: in pubspec.yaml Defaults and limits (playback speeds, Up Next countdown and more) lib/core/constants/constant.dart Logo, coin, VIP badge, company logo the files in assets/branding/ (same names) Icons lib/core/constants/app_icons.dart API paths, if yours differ lib/core/network/api_endpoints.dart English texts assets/l10n/template.json

The accent colours the app's buttons, switches, progress and highlights. Set your brand colour in Admin Panel › Settings › Branding › Theme colour: pick a ready-made one or type any hex code. The app, the panels and the website all pick it up, with no new app release. Try one below: GreenlightEmberIrisRoséAqua+ Episode 12 · LockedUnlock with coinsWatch one ad instead Episode 12 · LockedUnlock with coinsWatch one ad instead Greenlight: #C6EB3B on dark, #4A7300 on light. defaultAccent in lib/app/config/app_config.dart is the accent used until the app first reaches the server. It is one of the five accents drawn in theme_colors.dart, each with a deeper partner for light backgrounds.

All colours are in one file, lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dartCopy. Screens never use raw colours, so changing a value here changes it everywhere. Group What it colours coin, coinGradient, onCoin, coinShade Coins, prices and balances, and the gold Top up buttons vip, vipGradient, onVip VIP badges, the VIP card and VIP buttons like, streak Hearts, and the check-in streak dark… The dark theme (the default), on a pure black background light… The light theme greenlight, ember, iris, rose, aqua and their …OnLight partners The five accents. The OnLight colour is a deeper shade used on light backgrounds so text stays readable. The launcher icon, splash and notification colour are read by the phone before Flutter starts: see Logo, icons and splash.

The app uses Geist for text and Instrument Serif (italic) for big headings. 1 Add the font files Put your font's .ttf files in assets/fonts/<YourFont>/. 2 List them in pubspec.yaml pubspec.yaml fonts: - family: YourFont fonts: - asset: assets/fonts/YourFont/YourFont-Regular.ttf weight: 400 - asset: assets/fonts/YourFont/YourFont-Bold.ttf weight: 700 3 Use the family name lib/core/theme/app_typography.dart abstract final class AppFonts { static const String sans = 'YourFont'; static const String serif = 'InstrumentSerif'; }

eDrama's link setup is its own, so follow this page rather than the common guide. Two kinds of links open the app: Links Domain Paths Share links, made by the app Your backend's domain (shareBaseUrl) /s/… (a series), /c/… (a creator) Website links Your website's domain /series/…, /creators/…, and /s/…, /c/…

1 The share domain shareBaseUrl in lib/app/config/app_config.dart (App settings). 2 Android In android/app/build.gradle.kts, set both hosts (no https://): android/app/build.gradle.kts manifestPlaceholders["shareHost"] = "admin.your-domain.com" manifestPlaceholders["websiteHost"] = "your-domain.com" AndroidManifest.xml already uses them, with the paths above. 3 iOS In ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements, list both domains under Associated Domains: ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements <string>applinks:admin.your-domain.com</string> <string>applinks:your-domain.com</string> Turn on Associated Domains for your App ID in the Apple Developer portal too.

Phones check a file on each domain before they open links in your app: Backend: set EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE, EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 and EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID in its .env. See Admin Panel › Share links. Website: it serves the same files from your backend's app settings by itself.

Open https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json and /.well-known/apple-app-site-association: they show your app. On Android, after installing a release build: Settings › Apps › your app › Open by default lists your domains as verified. Send yourself a share link and tap it: the app opens on that series.

The app uses Firebase for sign-in (Authentication), push notifications (Cloud Messaging), Analytics, Crashlytics and App Check. Use one Firebase project for the app, the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal.

Follow the common guide to create the project, install the Firebase CLI and run flutterfire configure: 👉 Common guide › Firebase setup In eDrama, flutterfire configure writes three files. Replace the ones that ship with the app: File Platform lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart Both android/app/google-services.json Android ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist iOS Run it from the project folder after you change the package name.
