documents.t: Firebase console › Authentication › Sign-in method: Provider Used for Anonymous Guest mode: viewers watch before signing in. Required. Google Sign in with Google Apple Sign in with Apple (needed on iOS when Google is offered) Phone Phone sign-in. Needs the Blaze plan: common guide › Firebase billing. Email/Password Email sign-in, with a verified address Turn off any method you don't use in app_config.dart (signInWithGoogle, signInWithApple, signInWithPhone, signInWithEmail). Phone sign-in also follows the Phone sign-in switch in Admin Panel › Settings › App & support. For Google sign-in on Android, add your app's SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints (debug, upload and Play App Signing keys) in Firebase › Project settings › your Android app, then download google-services.json again.
Add the Project ID, Service account JSON, Web API key and Auth domain in Admin Panel › Settings › Notifications: Firebase and notifications.

App Check proves requests come from your real app. The app uses Play Integrity on Android and App Attest (with DeviceCheck as a fallback) on iOS in release builds, and the debug providers in debug builds. 1 Register the apps Firebase console › App Check › Apps: register the Android app with Play Integrity and the iOS app with App Attest. 2 Add debug tokens for testing A debug build prints a debug token in its log on first run. Add it in App Check › your app › Manage debug tokens. 3 Turn it on in the backend In the backend's .env, start with EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=monitor (requests without a valid token are only logged). When your released app works, switch to enforce, then run php artisan config:clear. caution Don't use enforce until the release build from the store passes App Check, or older builds and test devices will be refused.

eDrama does this differently from most apps: the app ships with English only, and every other language is a JSON file you upload in the Admin Panel. The app downloads it at its next start, so you can add a language or fix a word without releasing a new version.

Everything happens in Admin Panel › Settings › Regions & languages: add the language, download the Sample JSON, translate it, upload it and turn it on. Step by step: Regions and languages. Right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu) turn the app's layout around. Keys a file leaves out stay in English. A fresh install already lists Hindi as offered. Upload its file, or turn it off, before you launch. followDeviceLanguage in app_config.dart starts the app in the phone's language when it's offered; otherwise viewers get your default language.

The English texts are in assets/l10n/template.jsonCopy: one "key": "text" pair per line. Change the text, never the key, and keep words in braces such as {name} as they are. The same file is the Sample JSON the Admin Panel offers for translating.

Replace these files in assets/branding/, keeping the same names and formats: File What it is edrama_logo_dark.png The full logo for dark backgrounds edrama_logo_light.png The full logo for light backgrounds edrama_mark.png The mark alone coin.svg, coin_mono.svg The coin, in colour and in one colour vip.svg, vip_mono.svg The VIP badge company_logo.svg, company_logo_light.svg Your company's logo at the foot of the splash

The project is set up for flutter_launcher_icons. Replace the four files in assets/branding/launcher/ (same names), then run: dart run flutter_launcher_icons File What it is ic_launcher.png The full icon, for iOS and older Android ic_launcher_background.png The adaptive icon's background layer ic_launcher_foreground.png The adaptive icon's foreground. The files already leave Android's safe margin, so keep yours the same. ic_launcher_monochrome.png The one-colour layer for Android 13+ themed icons More about icon sizes and the options: common guide › App icon.

The first screen, drawn by the phone before the app starts: Android: android/app/src/main/res/drawable*/launch_background.xml and values*/styles.xml iOS: ios/Runner/Base.lproj/LaunchScreen.storyboard and the LaunchImage image set in Assets.xcassets The animated splash after it uses your logo from assets/branding/.

android/app/src/main/res/drawable-*/ic_stat_edrama.png: white on transparent, in each density folder. brand_green in android/app/src/main/res/values/brand_colors.xml: the colour Android tints it with.

The app ships as in.wrteam.edrama. Use your own, such as com.yourcompany.yourapp, before you set up Firebase or the stores: those are tied to it. Why it matters and how to pick one: common guide › Package name.

Where What to change android/app/build.gradle.kts namespace and applicationId android/app/src/main/kotlin/in/wrteam/edrama/MainActivity.kt Move it to folders matching your package (kotlin/com/yourcompany/yourapp/) and change its package line Xcode › Runner › Signing & Capabilities Bundle Identifier (PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER), and your own Team lib/app/config/app_config.dart appId The automatic way, from the common guide: dart pub add --dev change_app_package_name dart run change_app_package_name:main com.yourcompany.yourapp Check the four places above afterwards, and set appId yourself.

Firebase: add apps with the new IDs and run flutterfire configure again (Firebase). Admin Panel › Settings › Payments: Package name on the Google Play card and Bundle ID on the App Store card (Payments). Backend .env: EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE and EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID (Share links).

Pushes go from your server through Firebase Cloud Messaging. 1 Set up FCM and APNs Follow common guide › Notifications: google-services.json for Android, and for iOS the Push Notifications and Background Modes capabilities and an APNs key (.p8) uploaded to Firebase. 2 Add the Firebase keys to the Admin Panel Project ID and Service account JSON in Settings › Notifications (guide). 3 Make sure the background jobs run Pushes are sent by the queue.

The app sorts notifications into channels, so viewers can mute one kind in Android's settings: Channel Name drops New episodes account Account & purchases offers Offers quiet Quiet hours (silent) The small icon and its colour are in Logo, icons and splash.
Admin Panel › Audience › Push: send a push to every viewer or to one title's followers. It arrives in the app's inbox too.

App settings point at your server. Your own package name, Firebase files and AdMob app IDs. version: in pubspec.yaml raised for every release, such as 1.0.1+2. The number after + must go up each time. In Admin Panel › Settings › App & support, the Latest version and the Store link.

1 Create an upload key keytool -genkey -v -keystore upload-keystore.jks -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias upload Keep the file and its passwords safe: you need them for every update. 2 Create android/key.properties android/key.properties storePassword=your-store-password keyPassword=your-key-password keyAlias=upload storeFile=/full/path/to/upload-keystore.jks android/app/build.gradle.kts reads this file. Without it, release builds are signed with the debug key, which Google Play refuses.

The project includes a script that builds with obfuscation and keeps the debug symbols in build/debug-info: tool/build_release.sh appbundle # Google Play (.aab) tool/build_release.sh ipa # App Store tool/build_release.sh apk # a release APK Or with plain Flutter: flutter build appbundle and flutter build ipa.

Store listings, screenshots, review and release: common guide › Play Store and App Store. After the first Play release, copy the App signing key SHA-256 from Play Console › App integrity into the backend's EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256 (Share links) and into Firebase.

1 Open the project Unzip the app's code and open the folder in Android Studio or VS Code. 2 Get the packages flutter pub get For iOS, also run: cd ios pod install cd .. 3 Run it Start an emulator or connect a phone, then: flutter run The app talks to the server set in lib/app/config/app_config.dart. Until you change it, it shows WRTeam's demo server. Point it at your own Admin Panel next: App settings.

The project uses code generation for its models and state. The generated files are included, so you don't need this to run the app. If you edit a model or a provider, regenerate them: dart run build_runner build
flutter analyze flutter test
Follow the common guide to install Flutter, the Java JDK and your IDE: 👉 Flutter and Java JDK setup

eDrama is built and tested with Flutter 3.47.7. Use that exact version: a newer one may need code changes. flutter --version The project pins it in .fvmrc, so with FVM you can run fvm use in the project folder and then fvm flutter … instead of flutter ….
flutter doctor Fix anything it marks before you continue. For iOS you need a Mac with Xcode and CocoaPods.

VIP plans are auto-renewable subscriptions: the store charges the viewer again at the end of every period until they cancel. They are set up differently from coin packs, which are one-time consumable products (Ads and purchases). eDrama starts with three plans per region: weekly, monthly and yearly. For each plan you create a subscription in each store, then enter the store's IDs in Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›VIP plans. No free trials eDrama's VIP has no free trial and no introductory offer, a fair-play rule that the server enforces. Don't add trial or intro offers in either store. The Admin Panel also refuses a product ID, base plan ID or perk that names a trial, an intro offer or a "free week"/"7 days free".

Your app is created in Play Console and App Store Connect, with your own package name. Google Play: a payments profile is set up for your developer account, and an app build with billing has been uploaded to a testing track at least once. Play Console only lets you create products after that. App Store: the Paid Applications Agreement is signed, with your banking and tax details, in App Store Connect › Business. See the common in-app purchase guide for both.

On Google Play, a subscription holds one or more base plans. Each base plan has its own billing period and prices. eDrama stores both IDs for each VIP plan, so either layout works: One subscription with three base plans (for example subscription vip, base plans weekly, monthly, yearly), or three subscriptions, each with one base plan. 1 Create the subscription Play Console › your app › Monetize with Play › Products › Subscriptions › Create subscription. Enter a Product ID (such as vip; it can't change later) and a name. This is the Google Play subscription ID in eDrama. 2 Add a base plan In the subscription, Add base plan: Base plan ID: such as weekly. This is the Google Play base plan ID in eDrama. Type: Auto-renewing. Billing period: Weekly, Monthly or Yearly, matching the eDrama plan. Prices: set them per country. Google can fill other countries from one price. Save, then Activate the base plan. Repeat for the other two plans. 3 Leave offers empty Don't create offers (free trials or intro prices) on these base plans.

On the App Store, subscriptions live in a subscription group. A viewer can have only one subscription of a group at a time, and can move between them, so put all three VIP plans in one group. 1 Create the group App Store Connect › your app › Monetization › Subscriptions › Create a subscription group, such as VIP. Add a group localization (the name viewers see in their subscription settings). 2 Create a subscription for each plan In the group, Create a subscription: Reference Name: for you, such as VIP Weekly. Product ID: such as com.yourcompany.yourapp.vip.weekly. It can never be reused. This is the App Store product ID in eDrama. Subscription Duration: 1 Week, 1 Month or 1 Year, matching the eDrama plan. Subscription Prices: pick a price, and adjust other countries if you want. Localization: a display name and description. Review Information: a screenshot of the VIP screen and a short note for the reviewer. Repeat for the monthly and yearly plans. 3 Set the levels Drag the subscriptions into levels in the group, with your best-value plan at the top (often yearly). Apple uses the order for upgrades and downgrades. 4 Don't add introductory offers Leave Introductory Offers, Promotional Offers and Offer Codes empty. 5 Submit them with a build Your first subscriptions are reviewed with an app version: select them in the version's In-App Purchases and Subscriptions section before you submit it for review.

1 Enter the IDs Admin Panel›Money›Monetization, pick the region, open VIP plans, and Edit each plan: Field Value Price The price viewers pay in this region's currency, matching the store price Google Play subscription ID The subscription's Product ID Google Play base plan ID The base plan's ID App Store product ID The subscription's Product ID Perks What VIP includes, one per line (the default is "Every drama unlocked. No ads.") Offered in the app On Do this for every region you sell in. The store IDs are usually the same in every region, and the prices are per region. 2 Add the store keys and notifications Renewals, cancellations and refunds reach eDrama only through the stores' server notifications. Set up both in Settings › Payments: the Google Play keys with real-time developer notifications, and the App Store keys with the server notifications URL (version 2).

The viewer buys VIP in the app. The server checks the purchase with the store before VIP turns on. Each renewal, cancellation, refund or chargeback arrives from the store, and the viewer's VIP is extended or ended to match. eDrama reminds the viewer 24 hours before every renewal charge. Viewers cancel from the app's VIP screen, which opens the store's own subscription page. Subscribers and Auto-renew on for each plan show on the VIP plans tab. VIP revenue, after the store fee, shows on the Dashboard.

Store How Renewals Google Play Add License testers in Play Console › Settings › License testing, and install the app from a testing track Speeded up: a weekly or monthly plan renews about every 5 minutes, a yearly one about every 30 minutes App Store Sign in with a Sandbox account (App Store Connect › Users and Access › Sandbox) on a TestFlight or development build. Set the App Store card's Environment to Sandbox. Speeded up: 1 week ≈ 3 minutes, 1 month ≈ 5 minutes, 1 year ≈ 1 hour After a few renewals, the test subscription shows on the viewer in Admin Panel›Audience›Users, with Auto-renew on.

documents.t: The website is a Next.js app that you host separately from the Admin Panel, for example on Vercel. It has no database of its own. It reads your backend's public website API (/api/v1/website…), which holds no viewer data and needs no keys. Everything it shows is edited in Admin Panel›Content›Website: sections, layouts, texts, header and footer, theme, languages, search text and social links. The name, logos and theme colour come from Admin Panel›Settings›Branding, so the app, the panels and the website always match. Series are shown, never played. Every poster and button leads to the app. Pages are built once and shared by every visitor, then rebuilt in the background every 5 minutes. When you Publish in the Admin Panel, the backend tells the website to refresh at once. If your backend can't be reached, the website keeps showing its last good copy.

1 Install the Admin Panel first The website needs a running backend. See Admin Panel › Installation. 2 Run the website on your computer Requirements and local setup. 3 Connect it to your Admin Panel Connect to the Admin Panel: the server address, the website address and the refresh secret. 4 Put it live Deploy to Vercel, or any Node.js server. 5 Fill in the content Edit the website from the Admin Panel, then Publish.
documents.s: Set it up in this order

documents.t: Address What runs there your-domain.com (or www.) This website admin.your-domain.com The backend, Admin Panel and Creator Portal

The website and the Admin Panel need to know about each other: the website needs your server's address, to read its content; the Admin Panel needs the website's address, to show previews and to tell it about changes. The two share a refresh secret, so only your Admin Panel can ask the website to refresh.

They go in .env.local on your computer, or in your host's environment variables (on Vercel: Settings › Environment Variables). Variable Needed What it is EDRAMA_API_URL Yes Your backend's address without /api, such as https://admin.your-domain.com. Must be https:// (plain http:// only works for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and *.test). REVALIDATE_SECRET Recommended The refresh secret from the Admin Panel (below). Without it, a publish shows on the website within 5 minutes instead of at once. It must be at least 32 characters, which the Admin Panel's secret always is. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL No The website's own address, used only while the Admin Panel has none set. EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS No Extra hosts images may come from, comma-separated, when your files live on a CDN or an S3 bucket, for example my-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com,cdn.your-domain.com. Your backend's host is always allowed. EDRAMA_SCRIPT_HOSTS No Extra https:// origins allowed to serve analytics scripts, for self-hosted Plausible or Umami. Plausible, Umami Cloud and Google Analytics are allowed already. EDRAMA_FRAME_ORIGINS No Other addresses your Admin Panel opens at, comma-separated, that may show the website's live preview. Your backend's own address always may. Using S3 for files? If you moved files to Amazon S3 or another S3-compatible bucket in Admin Panel›Settings›Storage & video, add the bucket's host (or its Public URL host) to EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS, or posters won't show on the website.

1 Open the Connection tab Go to Admin Panel›Content›Website and open the Connection & history tab. It shows This server's address for the website (EDRAMA_API_URL): that is the value for EDRAMA_API_URL. 2 Set the Website address In Website address, enter where visitors open the website, such as https://www.your-domain.com, and click Save address. Changing it, and making a secret, needs a role that can edit Settings. It is used for previews, canonical links, the sitemap and share pictures, and to tell the website about changes. 3 Make the refresh secret Click Make a new secret. The secret is shown once: copy it and paste it into the website's REVALIDATE_SECRET. Then redeploy (or restart) the website so it reads the new value.

Change a heading on the Sections tab and click Publish. Open the website. The new heading shows within a minute. If it only shows after about 5 minutes, the secret doesn't match: make a new one and paste it again.

Each time you publish, the backend sends POST <Website address>/api/revalidate with a small JSON body, signed with the refresh secret (X-Edrama-Signature header). The website refuses calls that aren't signed with its REVALIDATE_SECRET or are more than 5 minutes old. If the call fails, nothing breaks: pages rebuild by themselves every 5 minutes.
Vercel is the easiest place to run the website: it builds Next.js apps with no server to manage, and its free Hobby plan is enough to start (check Vercel's own terms for commercial use).
A Vercel account. The website's code in a Git repository you own (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket), or the Vercel CLI on your computer. Your Admin Panel installed and reachable over https://.

1 Create the project In Vercel, click Add New › Project and import the website's repository. Vercel detects Next.js by itself (the repository's vercel.json says so too). No build settings need changing. 2 Add the settings Before the first deploy, open Environment Variables and add the variables from Connect to the Admin Panel, at least EDRAMA_API_URL and REVALIDATE_SECRET. Add them for Production and Preview. 3 Deploy Click Deploy. From now on every push to main deploys the live site, and every other branch gets its own preview address. 4 Add your domain In the project, open Settings › Domains, add your domain (for example your-domain.com and www.your-domain.com) and point its DNS records at Vercel exactly as that screen shows. 5 Tell the Admin Panel Set the same address in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Connection & history › Website address.
Open your domain: the home page shows your sections. Open https://your-domain.com/sitemap.xml and https://your-domain.com/robots.txt to see the files search engines read.

The website includes scripts/deploy.sh, which uses the Vercel CLI: npm install --global vercel vercel link # once: link the folder to your Vercel project scripts/deploy.sh # a preview deployment, with its own address scripts/deploy.sh --prod # the live site It runs npm ci, npm run lint and npm run build before deploying.

The website's .github/workflows/deploy.yml checks every push (lint, type check, npm audit) and can deploy to Vercel too. To turn the deploy on, add three repository secrets: Secret Where to find it VERCEL_TOKEN vercel.com/account/tokens VERCEL_ORG_ID .vercel/project.json after vercel link VERCEL_PROJECT_ID .vercel/project.json after vercel link Without VERCEL_TOKEN the workflow only runs the checks, so it works alongside Vercel's own Git connection. Use one or the other for deploys, not both.

Everything on the website is edited in Admin Panel›Content›Website. A live preview sits beside the form and shows what the form holds now, on a computer or a phone, in any language. Who can edit it Members with View on Schedule & Home can open this page, and Edit is needed to change it. The Website address and the refresh secret need Settings › Edit. See Team and roles. The Sections tab. The live preview sits to the right of the form.

Action What it does Save draft Keeps your changes. Visitors don't see them. Preview Opens the saved draft on your real website for 30 minutes. Nothing is published. Publish Makes the draft live. Visitors see it within a minute. You can write what changed. Discard draft Throws away unpublished changes and goes back to the live version. Switch website off / on Off shows visitors a short "back soon" page and asks search engines not to index it. Every publish is kept in Connection & history. Load into draft brings an earlier version back so you can check it and publish it again.

The home page is a list of sections you add, reorder, hide and style. Each section type has several Style choices. Section What it shows Top slider Big pictures with your headline and buttons. Picks your most popular series by itself, or shows slides you make. Numbers Series, episodes, categories and creators counted from your catalogue, or numbers you type. Series showcase A row or grid of series: new, popular, Top 10, complete, one category, one creator, or ones you pick. What is it? A few lines about your app, with feature points and phone pictures. Categories Your categories with their artwork, each leading to its category page. Get the app Store buttons, a direct APK link and a QR code. Always on the page. Creators Creators with live series, and an invitation to become one. Questions Questions and short answers. Search engines and AI assistants read these too. Call to action A bold band with a heading and a button. Text block A heading, a few paragraphs and an optional picture. In headings, put *stars* around a word or two to set them in the accent style. In text, **bold**, *italic* and [links](https://…) work.
The header style (Floating, Classic, Centred, Minimal), the footer style (Columns, Big name, Compact, Download first) and your Social links, shown as icons in the footer of every page.
The theme (Midnight (dark), Paper (light) or Follow the visitor's device), heading style, corners and motion, and which languages the website comes in. See Languages and app links.

Pick a language, then type each text in it. A box left empty shows the default language's text. Keep words in braces or after a colon, such as {app_name} or :count, exactly as they are: they are filled in for you.

Search engines and sharing: site title, description, share picture, whether search engines may index the site, whether AI crawlers may read it, llms.txt, and Google and Bing verification codes. Page by page: an optional search title, description and share picture for each kind of page (home, all series, all categories, each series, each category, each creator), in each language. Analytics: Plausible, Umami or Google Analytics. Google Analytics loads only after the visitor agrees.
The Website address, the refresh secret and the publish history. See Connect to the Admin Panel.

On the website Set in App name, logos, theme colour Admin Panel›Settings›Branding Google Play and App Store buttons Admin Panel›Settings›App & support › App versions › Store link Series, categories, creators Admin Panel›Content›Titles, Admin Panel›Content›Categories, Admin Panel›Community›Creators Legal pages in the footer Admin Panel›Settings›Legal pages Sample series While a series section has fewer than 4 live series, sample series fill it so the page never looks empty. Turn this off when your catalogue is ready.

The default language is at plain addresses: /series/…, /categories/…. Every other language turned on in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Look & languages lives under its code: /hi/series/…, /ar/series/…. Right-to-left languages such as Arabic are laid out right to left. Visitors switch language, and light or dark, from the header. Website texts are translated on the Translations tab. Series and category names use the translations already entered for the app. The sitemap lists every page in every language, with links between the language versions.

The website serves the two files phones read to open links in your app instead of the browser: /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android) /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS) Both are filled from your backend's app settings, so they stay empty until the backend knows your app (see Admin Panel › Share links). Your app must list the website's domain too: see Mobile App › Deep links. The app's own share links (/s/<id> for a series, /c/<handle> for a creator) also work on the website: they redirect to the series or creator page.

Address Page / Home, built from your sections /series All series, with category chips /series/<slug> One series: banner, poster, synopsis, creator, an Open in app button and store buttons /categories and /categories/<slug> All categories, and the series in one /creators/<slug> A creator's profile and series /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt For search engines /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt For AI assistants, only when you allow AI crawlers and llms.txt

Node.js 20 or newer (nodejs.org). Check with node -v. npm, which comes with Node.js. The website ships with a package-lock.json. A running eDrama backend. On your computer that can be the Admin Panel at http://localhost:8000. The website is built with Next.js 16 and React 19.

1 Open the website folder Open the website's source code (it comes with your purchase) in a terminal or in an editor such as VS Code. 2 Install the packages npm install 3 Create your settings file cp .env.example .env.local Open .env.local and set at least EDRAMA_API_URL. All settings are explained on Connect to the Admin Panel. .env.local EDRAMA_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 4 Start it npm run dev Open http://localhost:3000.
The home page shows your app name and the sections from Admin Panel›Content›Website.

A plain "eDrama" page with no sections. The website couldn't reach the backend. Check EDRAMA_API_URL: it is the server's address without /api, and it must start with https://. Plain http:// is accepted only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and *.test hosts. A "back soon" page. The website is switched off in the Admin Panel. Use Switch website on in Admin Panel›Content›Website.
npm run lint npm run build

The website is a standard Next.js app, so it runs on any server with Node.js 20 or newer: a VPS, a cloud VM, or a host with Node.js app support. It can't be a static export The website needs a running Node.js process: it rebuilds pages in the background, answers the refresh call and serves /.well-known files. Uploading the build folder to plain shared hosting won't work.

1 Build it npm ci npm run build Set the environment variables from Connect to the Admin Panel first, in .env.local or the server's environment. EDRAMA_API_URL is read when the site builds and when it runs. 2 Start it npm run start It listens on port 3000. Use PORT=8080 npm run start for another port. 3 Keep it running Use a process manager such as PM2 or a systemd service so it restarts after a crash or a reboot. 4 Put it behind HTTPS Point your web server (Nginx, Apache, Caddy) at the Node.js port as a reverse proxy, with an SSL certificate for your domain. Nginx example server { server_name your-domain.com www.your-domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; } } Then set the Website address in the Admin Panel, as on Connect to the Admin Panel.
